overview: Realty Income Corporation, founded in 1969 and known as 'The Monthly Dividend Company,' is the largest net-lease REIT in the US, owning and leasing a diversified portfolio of over 15,500 freestanding commercial properties across all 50 US states, the UK, and eight other European countries. The company acts as a full-service real estate capital provider, acquiring single-tenant retail, industrial, gaming, and (increasingly) data center properties under long-term net leases, and has declared 674 consecutive monthly dividends while raising the payout for 31+ consecutive years (S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrat).

business_model.summary: Realty Income generates rental income from long-term (typically 10-20 year) triple-net leases in which tenants bear property taxes, insurance, and maintenance, producing highly predictable, contractual cash flow with built-in rent escalators. Growth comes from external acquisitions funded by a low cost of capital (equity and investment-grade debt), supplemented by a fast-growing private capital/investment management platform (joint ventures with Apollo, KKR, GIC, Digital Realty, and Cloud Capital) that generates capital-light fee income.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — approximately 1,600 commercial tenants across roughly 92 industries, including large national/international retail, convenience, grocery, home-improvement, dollar-store, and industrial operators
business_model.geographic_mix: US ~90%, UK and continental Europe (8+ countries) ~10% and growing via European joint ventures (e.g., KKR Euro-denominated JV)

main_competitors: Spirit Realty Capital (acquired by Realty Income in 2024)
STORE Capital (acquired by GIC/Oak Street in 2023)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest net-lease REIT globally by enterprise value (~$80-90B) and property count (15,500+); roughly 3-4x the size of its next-largest direct peer (W.P. Carey)

moat_factors.description: A3/A- investment-grade credit ratings give access to unsecured debt at ~67.5 bps over SOFR; scale allows Realty Income to win larger sale-leaseback and portfolio deals that smaller peers cannot underwrite
~1,600 tenants across 92 industries and multiple property types/geographies reduces single-tenant and sector concentration risk relative to smaller net-lease peers
55+ year operating history, 674 consecutive monthly dividends, and Dividend Aristocrat status support premium access to equity capital markets
Realty Income Investment Management (joint ventures with Apollo, KKR, GIC, Digital Realty, Cloud Capital) creates a capital-light, higher-ROE growth avenue that peers largely lack at scale
Long lease terms (10-20 years) and sale-leaseback structures lock in tenants, but leases eventually roll and re-leasing risk exists

weaknesses: Heavy exposure to brick-and-mortar retail tenants vulnerable to e-commerce disruption and consumer-discretionary pressure
Exposure to troubled/lower-credit tenants (e.g., dollar stores, drugstores) that have faced bankruptcy or restructuring risk in recent years
Large size makes it harder to move the needle on growth without very large acquisition volumes ($10B+ annually)
AFFO per share growth has slowed to low-single-digit/mid-single-digit range versus faster-growing smaller peers

growth_drivers: Elevated acquisition volume guidance of ~$10 billion for FY2026 (raised from $9.5 billion), funded by a mix of public equity, debt, and private capital

Expansion into industrial and digital infrastructure — a new $6 billion programmatic hyperscale data center joint venture with Cloud Capital (Realty Income investing up to $1.4 billion for a 45% stake) plus an existing Digital Realty build-to-suit JV

Growth of the Investment Management private capital platform (Apollo, KKR, GIC joint ventures) generating capital-light fee income and broadening the addressable market beyond Realty Income's own balance sheet

Continued European expansion (UK and eight other European countries) diversifying geographic exposure and tapping a large, under-penetrated net-lease market (management cites a combined US/European addressable market near $15 trillion)
Contractual rent escalators embedded in existing leases providing organic same-store rent growth with high (~98.8%) occupancy and rent-recapture rates above 100% on re-leased space
Potential further consolidation of the fragmented net-lease sector (Realty Income has a history of large M&A, e.g., Spirit Realty Capital acquisition completed in 2024, VEREIT acquisition in 2021)

business.description: Dollar General (~3.3% of ABR), 7-Eleven (~3.1%), and Walgreens (~3.0%) are the largest tenants; top 20 tenants are ~32% of ABR. Several historical tenants (Rite Aid, Red Lobster, Walgreens) have faced bankruptcy/restructuring, creating re-leasing and bad-debt risk
~73% of rental revenue from retail tenants exposes the portfolio to e-commerce disruption, discretionary spending downturns, and store closures
At an ~$80-90B enterprise value, Realty Income must deploy very large capital amounts annually to sustain meaningful per-share AFFO growth, increasing reliance on capital markets access

financial.description: Reported net debt/EBITDA of 5.74x and interest coverage of only 2.35x (per info.json screen data) are weaker than typical investment-grade REIT targets (closer to 5-5.5x and 3x+), making the balance sheet more sensitive to refinancing costs and ratings pressure

REIT business model depends on continuous access to debt and equity markets; higher-for-longer rates raise the cost of refinancing maturing debt and new acquisition funding, compressing the spread between acquisition cap rates and cost of capital
UK/European operations (GBP/EUR denominated rents and JV equity) create FX translation risk, partially hedged

regulatory.description: Must maintain REIT status (distribute 90%+ of taxable income), limiting retained capital for growth and tying dividend policy to taxable income rules

regulatory.risk: Property tax and local regulatory changes
regulatory.description: Net-lease structure passes most property-level regulatory/tax costs to tenants, but widespread tenant-side cost increases could pressure tenant credit quality

macro.description: As a high-yield, capital-intensive REIT, Realty Income's valuation and cost of equity are highly sensitive to the level and trajectory of long-term interest rates

While many tenants are 'recession-resistant' (convenience, grocery, dollar stores), a broad consumer-spending downturn or recession could increase vacancy and bad debt across the retail-heavy portfolio
Cap rate expansion/compression cycles directly affect acquisition yields, portfolio valuations, and the spread economics underlying AFFO growth

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Net-lease REIT sector outlook has improved in 2026 amid anticipated Federal Reserve rate cuts, which narrow the cap-rate/cost-of-capital spread and support acquisition-driven growth; institutional interest in net-lease real estate (including via Realty Income's own private capital vehicles) remains robust
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate — long-duration leases and diversified, largely defensive tenant mix (grocery, convenience, drug, dollar stores) dampen cyclicality versus other commercial real estate, though acquisition volume and cap rates are cyclical with interest rates
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — both as a bond-proxy equity (dividend yield competes with risk-free rates) and operationally (cost of debt/equity capital for acquisitions)
key_input_costs: Cost of debt capital (credit spreads, SOFR)
Cost of equity capital (share price/dividend yield)

recent_developments.event: AFFO per share grew 3.8% YoY to $1.09; revenue of ~$1.55B beat estimates; portfolio occupancy 98.8% with rent recapture rates above 100%
Raised FY2026 investment volume guidance to ~$10 billion (from $9.5 billion) and raised FY2026 AFFO per share guidance to $4.44-$4.45 (from $4.41-$4.44)

Announced $6 billion programmatic hyperscale data center joint venture with Cloud Capital; Realty Income to invest up to $1.4 billion for a 45% equity interest across Northern Virginia data center assets (under 400MW capacity)

Expanded private capital/investment management platform: Core Plus Fund reached ~$3.27B AUM after $1.7B of new institutional commitments (March 2026); Apollo joint venture brought in $1B of permanent equity for a 49% interest; KKR Euro-denominated JV (€528M) for a 49% interest in a European portfolio; GIC $1.5B US industrial build-to-suit JV
Raised the monthly dividend for the third time in 2026 (to $0.2710/share, ~136th increase since 1994), extending the 31+ year dividend growth streak
Recast and expanded credit facilities to $5.38 billion, improving liquidity and financial flexibility
Industrial now represents ~65% of quarterly global real estate investment activity, reflecting the strategic pivot toward industrial/digital infrastructure alongside legacy retail

items.notes: Raised from prior guidance of $4.41-$4.44; implies ~4% growth at the midpoint versus FY2025 AFFO per share
Raised from $9.5 billion, driven by a robust deal pipeline including the Cloud Capital data center JV
Portfolio occupancy was 98.8% at Q2 2026 with rent recapture rates above 100% on re-leased space

items.target: up to $1.4 billion (45% equity interest in $6B JV)
items.notes: New Cloud Capital programmatic hyperscale data center venture announced alongside Q2 2026 results

guidance.management_commentary: Management emphasized continued momentum in deal sourcing (industrial now ~65% of quarterly investment activity), the strategic shift toward industrial and digital infrastructure, and the growing contribution of the capital-light private capital/investment management platform (Apollo, KKR, GIC joint ventures) to per-share growth. Leadership reiterated confidence in sustaining the 31+ year dividend growth streak while targeting mid-single-digit AFFO per share growth.

bull_case: Largest, most diversified net-lease REIT with investment-grade credit ratings (A3/A-) providing a durable cost-of-capital advantage over smaller peers in a fragmented, consolidating industry
674 consecutive monthly dividends and 31+ years of dividend increases (Dividend Aristocrat) appeal to income-focused investors, with the dividend raised again in 2026

New growth vectors — data center/digital infrastructure joint ventures (Cloud Capital, Digital Realty) and a fast-scaling private capital management platform (Apollo, KKR, GIC) — diversify beyond legacy retail and can be capital-light, higher-ROE growth
Raised FY2026 guidance (AFFO per share and investment volume) signals continued execution and an improving acquisition environment as rate cuts narrow cap-rate spreads
High occupancy (98.8%) and above-100% rent recapture rates demonstrate resilient demand for Realty Income's real estate even amid pockets of retail tenant distress
bear_case: Leverage metrics (net debt/EBITDA ~5.7x, interest coverage ~2.35x) are weaker than ideal for the rating category, leaving limited cushion if rates stay elevated or credit spreads widen

Heavy legacy exposure to brick-and-mortar retail (~73% of rental revenue) carries ongoing tenant bankruptcy/restructuring risk (e.g., dollar stores, drugstores, casual dining) that can pressure occupancy and bad debt

Scale is a double-edged sword: Realty Income must deploy very large annual capital ($10B+) just to sustain mid-single-digit AFFO per share growth, making growth increasingly dependent on capital markets access and deal competition

High dividend yield and REIT structure make the stock a bond-proxy that is highly sensitive to the path of long-term interest rates; a reacceleration in rates or inflation could pressure the share price and cost of equity

Diversification into unfamiliar asset classes (data centers, European markets) via joint ventures introduces new execution, partner, and underwriting risk outside the company's historical retail net-lease core competency
